name: Deployable UltraFlex Solar Wings
title: Deployable UltraFlex Solar Wings
shortDescription: Accordion-fold solar arrays that unfold into circular or rectangular wings after orbital injection. They use advanced multi-junction GaAs cells to deliver over 300 W/kg specific power.
description: Accordion-fold solar arrays that unfold into circular or rectangular wings after orbital injection. They use advanced multi-junction GaAs cells to deliver over 300 W/kg specific power.
engineeringSpecification: Circular, accordion-fold fan-like solar arrays developed by Northrop Grumman. Utilizing lightweight, multi-junction gallium arsenide (GaAs) photovoltaic cells stretched over flexible structural gores, they unfold into a rigid circular wing after orbital injection, delivering over 300 W/kg specific power.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Offers an exceptional power-to-mass ratio and compact stowed volume compared to rigid panels. However, solar flux drops inversely with the square of the distance from the Sun (1/r^2), making them ineffective beyond Jupiter's orbit or during prolonged planetary eclipses without heavy battery banks.

name: Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG)
title: Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG)
shortDescription: Contains 4.8 kg of Plutonium-238 dioxide in solid ceramic pellets. As the plutonium decays naturally, it generates heat; solid-state thermocouples convert this directly into continuous electricity.
description: Contains 4.8 kg of Plutonium-238 dioxide in solid ceramic pellets. As the plutonium decays naturally, it generates heat; solid-state thermocouples convert this directly into continuous electricity.
engineeringSpecification: Contains 4.8 kg of Plutonium-238 dioxide in solid ceramic pellets. As the plutonium undergoes natural alpha decay, it generates approximately 2,000 watts of thermal heat, which solid-state lead-telluride thermocouples convert directly into continuous electrical power without moving parts.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Provides uninterrupted, weather-independent electrical and thermal power day and night, regardless of distance from the Sun. The trade-off is high cost, strict nuclear launch safety protocols, low thermal-to-electric conversion efficiency (~6%), and gradual power decay (~0.8% per year).

name: Ka-Band Phased Array Antenna
title: Ka-Band Phased Array Antenna
shortDescription: Operating at 32 GHz, Ka-band frequencies carry four times more information per second than legacy X-band signals. The phased array allows electronic beam steering without mechanical gimbals.
description: Operating at 32 GHz, Ka-band frequencies carry four times more information per second than legacy X-band signals. The phased array allows electronic beam steering without mechanical gimbals.
engineeringSpecification: Operating at 32 GHz (deep space) or 26 GHz (near-Earth), this electronically steered antenna array uses phase shifters across hundreds of micro-emitters to focus high-frequency radio beams without mechanical gimbals, carrying up to four times more data than legacy X-band systems.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Shorter wavelengths enable narrow beamwidths and massive bandwidth from compact apertures, while electronic steering eliminates mechanical vibration. However, high-frequency Ka-band signals suffer severe atmospheric attenuation (rain fade) on Earth and demand ultra-precise spacecraft pointing accuracy (<0.1°).

name: Low Lunar Polar Orbit
title: Low Lunar Polar Orbit
shortDescription: A 50 km circular orbit passing directly over the Moon's north and south poles. As the Moon rotates beneath the orbiter over 27.3 days, the spacecraft achieves 100% global surface coverage.
description: A 50 km circular orbit passing directly over the Moon's north and south poles. As the Moon rotates beneath the orbiter over 27.3 days, the spacecraft achieves 100% global surface coverage.
engineeringSpecification: A circular orbital trajectory at an altitude of 50 km inclined at ~90°, passing directly over the Moon's north and south poles. As the Moon rotates beneath the orbital plane over a 27.3-day sidereal period, the spacecraft achieves 100% global surface coverage.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Low altitude maximizes instrument spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio, while polar inclination grants access to Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) containing water ice. Conversely, localized lunar mass concentrations ('mascons') perturb the orbit, requiring frequent station-keeping delta-v burns to prevent surface impact.

name: Laser Altimeter (LOLA / ATLAS)
title: Laser Altimeter (LOLA / ATLAS)
shortDescription: Fires pulsed laser beams at the ground and measures the round-trip travel time of reflected photons. Because it generates its own illumination, it maps permanently shadowed polar craters.
description: Fires pulsed laser beams at the ground and measures the round-trip travel time of reflected photons. Because it generates its own illumination, it maps permanently shadowed polar craters.
engineeringSpecification: Fires short, high-repetition pulsed Nd:YAG laser beams (1064 nm or 532 nm) toward the planetary surface and measures the round-trip time-of-flight of reflected photons with picosecond precision. Generates high-resolution 3D topographic elevation maps and surface slope models.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: As an active sensor, it operates independently of solar illumination, allowing 3D mapping inside pitch-black polar craters. Its narrow footprint provides centimeter-level vertical accuracy, but swath width is narrow, requiring months of orbital passes to build contiguous global terrain models.

name: Thermal & Epithermal Neutron Spectrometer
title: Thermal & Epithermal Neutron Spectrometer
shortDescription: Cosmic rays constantly strike planetary soil, knocking loose fast neutrons. When these neutrons collide with hydrogen atoms in subsurface water ice, they lose energy and slow down.
description: Cosmic rays constantly strike planetary soil, knocking loose fast neutrons. When these neutrons collide with hydrogen atoms in subsurface water ice, they lose energy and slow down.
engineeringSpecification: Detects secondary neutrons knocked loose from planetary regolith by galactic cosmic rays. By measuring the energy moderation of thermal and epithermal neutrons using Helium-3 gas proportional counters, it quantifies subsurface hydrogen concentrations down to 1 meter depth.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Neutrons interact strongly with hydrogen nuclei (which have nearly identical mass), making this instrument the gold standard for detecting buried water ice without digging. However, spatial resolution is inherently coarse (roughly equal to the spacecraft's orbital altitude, e.g., ~50 km footprint).

name: Subsurface Radar Sounder
title: Subsurface Radar Sounder
shortDescription: Transmits high-frequency radio waves into the ground. When the waves pass through boundaries between dry rock, porous soil, and subsurface ice layers, echoes reflect back to the orbiter.
description: Transmits high-frequency radio waves into the ground. When the waves pass through boundaries between dry rock, porous soil, and subsurface ice layers, echoes reflect back to the orbiter.
engineeringSpecification: Transmits low-to-high frequency radio waves (typically 15–60 MHz) via a long dipole antenna into the planetary crust. Echoes reflected from dielectric interfaces reveal buried geological strata, lava tubes, and deep subsurface water-ice deposits down to several kilometers.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Penetrates meters to kilometers beneath the surface where optical and neutron sensors cannot reach. The trade-off is the requirement for a massive deployable dipole antenna (10 to 40 meters long) and susceptibility to surface clutter from rough terrain.

shortDescription: A reusable two-stage rocket powered by liquid oxygen and rocket-grade kerosene (RP-1). It can lift over 22,800 kg to Low Earth Orbit.

title: 3D Stereo Mapping Camera
shortDescription: Twin optical cameras configured at offset viewing angles take simultaneous stereoscopic images of planetary surfaces to reconstruct high-resolution 3D elevation models.
description: Twin optical cameras configured at offset viewing angles take simultaneous stereoscopic images of planetary surfaces to reconstruct high-resolution 3D elevation models.
engineeringSpecification: Twin high-resolution panchromatic/multispectral optical cameras mounted at fixed forward and aft stereo viewing angles (~15°–25° off-nadir). Captures simultaneous overlapping image strips to reconstruct sub-meter Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) via photogrammetry.
physicsAndDesignTradeOff: Provides exceptional horizontal spatial resolution (down to 0.5 meters/pixel) for landing site hazard certification (boulders and slopes).
